summary: Intermittent Okta session swap prevents runbook approval flow for oncall tooling
description: Users intermittently receive 403/authorization failures when trying to approve runbook requests in the internal Runbook Console. The UI prompts for reauthentication but Okta reports the user still has an active session. Behavioral pattern suggests two different session contexts are being observed by the runbook service (session swap) which results in the approval token being rejected.
impact: Affects oncall engineers attempting to approve critical runbooks via the internal console and Electron runbook client. Approx 8-12 occurrences in the last 48 hours across US-East clusters; prevented at least three emergency mitigations from being executed within SLA windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to Runbook Console in Chrome (session A) via Okta SSO.
2) From the same machine, start Electron runbook client or CLI that initiates a separate SSO flow (session B) without fully clearing cookies/SSO state.
3) Trigger an approval flow in the Console (POST /api/v1/approvals).
4) Observe intermittent 403 with response body 'session-mismatch' or the UI asking to reauthenticate even though Okta shows active session.
Note: behavior is intermittent; reproduces more reliably when there is background automatic token refresh (Okta session refresh) occurring close to approval attempts.

investigation_notes: Observed correlation between Okta session refresh events and approval failures (strong temporal clustering around refresh timestamps).

Auth-proxy rotates session id by issuing Set-Cookie during POST okta/refresh; runbook-service validates approval tokens against a session id stored client-side which can be stale when rotation happens mid-flow.

Hypothesis A: race during session rotation where UI obtains an approval token bound to old session id while auth-proxy issues new session id to the browser, causing token validation to fail server-side.
Hypothesis B: load-balancer affinity change causes the initial session-binding validation to hit a different auth-proxy instance that does not yet have the rotated session mapping.
Initial telemetry: 11 incidents between 2026-03-10 16:00 and 2026-03-12 08:00; 9 of 11 show identical runbook-service error string 'session-owner-mismatch'.
Repro steps created and confirmed locally by reproducing with parallel SSO flows (Console + Electron).
Related config: Okta refresh interval in our SSO policy was changed 2026-03-09 (internal change request ID IDP-2026-03-09), which increased frequency of background refresh by ~30%.
Candidate fix: make session rotation atomic and coordinate approval-token issuance to use the new session id or defer rotation until outstanding approval flows complete.
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporarily reverted the session-rotation-from-refresh change in auth-proxy for prod us-east and added a short delay to cookie rotation to avoid mid-request swaps. Engineering PR (identity-proxy#842) will implement atomic rebind and include tests that exercise concurrent approval flows. Long-term: add end-to-end test in CI that simulates parallel SSO flows and enforce sticky-session invariants on the LB. Monitoring: added alert for 'runbook-service session-owner-mismatch' with 5-min burn rate. Pending: PR code review and staged rollout to prod (target 2026-03-15).
